messages:
marta: Quick update — I uploaded the new Llama3 variant weights for onboarding to gs://redwood-models/onboarding/llama3-v2/weights_v2.tar.gz. Please verify metadata and checksum.
raj: pulled it. tarball size looks normal. metadata.json inside only has {\"version\": \"v2\", \"license\": \"apache-2.0\"} — missing model_sha256 and source fields. failing config validator on my end.
cheng: that explains the serving bootstrap error I hit earlier. our loader enforces model_sha256 + origin.hf_repo to build the cache key.
marta: ack. I can re-upload with full metadata. do we have a preferred field name for hf repo? origin.hf_repo or repo_url?
raj: origin.hf_repo is what the backend expects atm (short and stable).
infra-bot: checksum job queued — job_id: chk_4021. results will post here when done. :gear:
sylvia: small tokenizer note while you're here — the chat templates for this model are adding a redundant <|bos|> token before the system prompt on generation start. observed with our vtokenizer 0.4.2.
oliver: :eyes: is that happening in streaming or only batch? saw a 1-token drift in streaming logs yesterday.
sylvia: both. repro steps: pass prompt {role:system, content: "You are a helpful assistant"} then user prompt. tokenizer.encode adds <|bos|> and our chat-fmt wrapper also inserts one. leads to off-by-one padding and odd attention masks.
cheng: do we have a quick patch? either ensure chat-fmt wrapper doesn't insert bos when tokenizer is configured with add_bos=false, or set vtokenizer default add_bos=false for chat mode.
marta: for onboarding let's make the model config explicit. include "tokenizer": {"add_bos": false, "special_tokens": {"bos": "<|bos|>", "eos": "<|eos|>"}} in metadata.json.
raj: +1. also include a quant_profile hint so autoscaler can pick int8-safe kernels: "quant_profile": "int8_wholeword_preferred".
infra-bot: checksum result: model_sha256=6b3f8a2c9f4d... short: 6b3f8a2c. uploaded metadata missing this — please update and re-upload. :white_check_mark:
marta: re-uploading now with metadata fields: model_sha256, origin.hf_repo, tokenizer.add_bos=false, quant_profile. pinging when complete.
oliver: small test suggestion: run this locally to sanity check tokenizer delta:
```
from vtokenizer import VTokenizer
t = VTokenizer('llama3-v2')
print(t.encode('')[:10])
```
check for duplicate bos token at start.
sylvia: also confirm chat template layering: our chatfmt should only wrap messages, not inject tokenizer-controlled tokens. code pointer: tools/chatfmt.py:line 42.
raj: once marta re-uploads I can run config-validator & a quick canary deploy to dev so we catch any runtime off-by-one before prod.
marta: done. new tar uploaded: gs://redwood-models/onboarding/llama3-v2/weights_v2_meta.tar.gz. metadata.json includes model_sha256 and tokenizer.add_bos=false. checksum matches infra-bot output.
infra-bot: canary deploy kicked: canary_775. watch logs at https://console.redwood/infra/canaries/775 :satellite:
cheng: running the tokenizer + generation smoke now. will report regressions.
raj: if all green can we add a small validator rule: if tokenizer.add_bos==false and chatfmt inserts bos -> warn. reduces manual back-and-forth.
oliver: agree — add a lint rule in onboarding pipeline. PR incoming from me tomorrow.
sylvia: thanks all. minor follow-ups: I'll open an issue about vtokenizer default semantics so we don't silently drift between versions. :memo:
marta: thanks, closing this check for now. ping here if you see anything odd during canary. :thumbsup:
